newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rain pushes prices down at Colombo tea auction.
newsitem.headline: Rain pushes prices down at Colombo tea auction.

text.p: Prices were down at the Colombo auction on Monday as more rain-affected lower quality teas arrived in the market, brokers said.
The island's distinct low-grown teas, popular with Russian and Middle Eastern buyers, held firm, but the more expensive high-growns declined due to poor quality, they said.
"There is a general lowering of quality mainly due to the rains," said Rohan Iddawela of brokerage Forbes and Walker.
Brokers say monsoon rains have boosted quantities while reducing quality.
This week's auction, reduced to one day from the usual two due to a Buddhist holiday, had 4.9 million kg on offer.

Most western high growns declined 3-6 rupees and BOP fannings dropped by 2-6, mostly on low quality, Forbes said. Most low growns saw good general demand while the leafy varieties were 2-4 rupees dearer, it said.
The anticipated gross auction average was 115 rupees ($1.97) per kg, compared to 115.66 last week, Forbes said.
The next auction is on May 27-28, when 5.7 million kg will be on offer.
